Macro Reading for Traders
Intermediate
Macro Reading for Traders

CPI, the Fed, the yield curve and the dollar — how the pieces connect.

Includes 5 lessons, quizzes, sources, and a completion badge. The $100,000 simulator supports spot instruments; options and futures contract mechanics are worksheet exercises.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

Your progress
0%
Earn the
Macro Reading Completion
badge on completion

An introduction to CPI releases, central-bank decisions, Treasury yields and the dollar index, with exercises for separating observed data from uncertain market interpretations.

What you'll be able to do
Read a CPI release and identify which component drove the surprise, rather than reacting to the headline number.
Explain how FOMC decisions are announced and why published expectations and other information may influence different market reactions.
Interpret the shape of the yield curve and describe what a flattening or inversion has historically signalled.
Connect dollar strength to the behaviour of commodities, emerging markets and large exporters.
Combine several macro signals into one written view instead of trading each release in isolation.
Before you start

No economics background is assumed. You should know what an interest rate is and be willing to read a data release rather than a summary of it. Each lesson links to the primary source — the statistical agency or the central bank itself — so you can check every figure yourself.

How the lessons build on each other

Start by reading CPI definitions and component changes. The Fed lesson then distinguishes policy announcements from expectations; inflation is one input among several. The yield-curve lesson compares maturities and model limitations. The dollar lesson considers currency translation and exposures without assuming a fixed price response. The final exercise compares several observations and alternative explanations.

Who this track is not for

This is not a macroeconomic forecasting course and it will not tell you where rates or inflation are going. It does not cover trading around releases with leverage, which is a specialist activity with execution risks that reading cannot prepare you for. If you want a directional call on the economy, no honest course can give you one.

Lessons
LESSON 1
Reading CPI and Inflation Data
CPI measures selected consumer-price changes. Read the release, its definitions and components without assuming a predictable market response.
8 min
LESSON 2
The Fed & FOMC Cycle — How Rates Get Set
The FOMC has eight regularly scheduled meetings a year, and its decisions can affect market expectations.
9 min
LESSON 3
The Yield Curve and Recession-Risk Research
Yield-curve inversion has historically been associated with elevated US recession risk, but timing varies and the signal is not a standalone forecast.
8 min
LESSON 4
The Dollar Index (DXY) — Reading Currency Context
DXY tracks the dollar against six currencies and offers context for studying currency exposure, with important limits.
7 min
LESSON 5
Putting It Together — A Macro Dashboard for Traders
Compare growth, inflation and financial indicators in a documented worksheet, without treating a regime label as a trading instruction.
8 min
Completion badge

Macro Reading Completion: Awarded after completing every lesson in the Macro Reading for Traders track. Educational simulation only — not financial advice.

All courses

Macro Reading for Traders

CPI, the Fed, the yield curve and the dollar — how the pieces connect.

Includes 5 lessons, quizzes, sources, and a completion badge. The $100,000 simulator supports spot instruments; options and futures contract mechanics are worksheet exercises.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

Macro Reading Completion
badge on completion

An introduction to CPI releases, central-bank decisions, Treasury yields and the dollar index, with exercises for separating observed data from uncertain market interpretations.

What you'll be able to do
Read a CPI release and identify which component drove the surprise, rather than reacting to the headline number.
Explain how FOMC decisions are announced and why published expectations and other information may influence different market reactions.
Interpret the shape of the yield curve and describe what a flattening or inversion has historically signalled.
Connect dollar strength to the behaviour of commodities, emerging markets and large exporters.
Combine several macro signals into one written view instead of trading each release in isolation.
Before you start

No economics background is assumed. You should know what an interest rate is and be willing to read a data release rather than a summary of it. Each lesson links to the primary source — the statistical agency or the central bank itself — so you can check every figure yourself.

How the lessons build on each other

Start by reading CPI definitions and component changes. The Fed lesson then distinguishes policy announcements from expectations; inflation is one input among several. The yield-curve lesson compares maturities and model limitations. The dollar lesson considers currency translation and exposures without assuming a fixed price response. The final exercise compares several observations and alternative explanations.

Who this track is not for

This is not a macroeconomic forecasting course and it will not tell you where rates or inflation are going. It does not cover trading around releases with leverage, which is a specialist activity with execution risks that reading cannot prepare you for. If you want a directional call on the economy, no honest course can give you one.

Lessons
LESSON 1
Reading CPI and Inflation Data
CPI measures selected consumer-price changes. Read the release, its definitions and components without assuming a predictable market response.
8 min
LESSON 2
The Fed & FOMC Cycle — How Rates Get Set
The FOMC has eight regularly scheduled meetings a year, and its decisions can affect market expectations.
9 min
LESSON 3
The Yield Curve and Recession-Risk Research
Yield-curve inversion has historically been associated with elevated US recession risk, but timing varies and the signal is not a standalone forecast.
8 min
LESSON 4
The Dollar Index (DXY) — Reading Currency Context
DXY tracks the dollar against six currencies and offers context for studying currency exposure, with important limits.
7 min
LESSON 5
Putting It Together — A Macro Dashboard for Traders
Compare growth, inflation and financial indicators in a documented worksheet, without treating a regime label as a trading instruction.
8 min
